stem:
Uday studies this pond food chain: algae → small insects → small fish → large fish → heron.

Which statement correctly assigns the trophic levels?

options.text: Algae are at the first trophic level, small insects at the second, small fish at the third, and the heron at a later level.
The heron is at the first trophic level because it is the largest animal in the chain.
The large fish is at the first trophic level because it is bigger and stronger than the insects.
Every organism in the pond is at the same trophic level because they share one pond.

teacher.key_rationale: Producers start at level one; each consumer steps up the chain. Ranking by body size is a surface cue. Putting a large fish first drops the producer-first rule. Treating the whole habitat as one level over-widens trophic level.
